items: Understand the 9-Month Regression Signs: Recognize that sudden frequent night wakings, nap refusals, shortened naps, and bedtime resistance indicate the 9-month regression rather than a sign you did something wrong as a parent.

Accept That This Regression Is Temporary: Understand that the 9-month sleep regression typically lasts 2-6 weeks and represents a temporary neurological event that will end, not a permanent change to your baby's sleep.

Identify Separation Anxiety as the Night Waking Cause: Understand that your baby's night wakings are driven by their new awareness of object permanence, making them anxious about you leaving and not returning during sleep.

Recognize Motor Milestone Practice During Sleep: Understand that your baby may be practicing new skills like crawling or pulling to stand during partial arousals between sleep cycles, causing position changes and distress.

Avoid Sleep Training During This Regression: Resist the urge to implement formal sleep training methods during this 2-6 week period, as your baby is neurologically incapable of consolidating sleep changes right now.

Make Only Temporary Schedule Adjustments: Adjust your baby's schedule temporarily to manage the disruption without making permanent changes, since your baby's underlying sleep needs have not actually changed.

Help Your Baby Return to a Comfortable Position: When your baby wakes crying after practicing motor milestones, help them return to a comfortable lying position so they can settle back to sleep more easily.

Manage the Nap Transition Overlap Carefully: Adjust nap timing to address overtiredness created by the transition from 3 naps to 2, recognizing that some schedule chaos is expected during this period.
Share Nighttime Duties with Your Partner: Coordinate with your partner to split night wakings and caregiving duties so neither of you bears the full burden of the exhaustion alone.
Prioritize Your Own Rest When Possible: Accept that surviving this regression requires you to rest when you can, even if that means letting some household tasks go undone temporarily.

Set Realistic Expectations With Your Support System: Communicate openly with your partner and support network about the 2-6 week timeline so everyone has realistic expectations and can offer appropriate support.

Focus on Protecting Your Sleep Foundation: Concentrate on not creating new sleep problems during this period rather than trying to solve existing ones, knowing the regression will pass and sleep will improve.
